figures.caption: Figure 1. Design of solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) with high conductivity and self-passivating stability. a) Schematic of anionic and cationic frameworks in the crystal structure of Li7PS6 and enhanced Li-ion conductivity through strategic anion modulation and cation substitution. b) Schematic of self-passivating stabilization mechanism between SSE and electrodes. Due to potential diﬀerence, spontaneous hazardous electron transfer is triggered between SSE and electrodes, leading to the formation of solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) and cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI). If the in situ formed SEI and CEI can remain stable and are characterized by ionic conduction and electronic insulation, the detrimental interfacial reactions can be eﬀectively suppressed. Through such a self-sacriﬁcial passivation strategy, the practical stability window of the SSE can be extended. particles.[16–18]
